html:
The Battle of Shanhai Pass was fought on 27 May 1644 at Shanhaiguan, where the Great Wall meets the sea, in today's Hebei province in northern China. The Manchu army of the Qing, let through the wall by the Ming general Wu Sangui, beat the rebel leader Li Zicheng. It opened China to Qing rule.

The Ming dynasty was failing from famine, unpaid armies and revolt. In April 1644 Li Zicheng's peasant army took Beijing, and the last Ming emperor hanged himself. Wu Sangui commanded the best Ming army left, at the pass that kept the Manchus out of China. Caught between Li and the Manchus, he chose the Manchus and asked their regent, Prince Dorgon, for help. Li marched on the pass with perhaps 60,000 men. Wu's troops fought him first and nearly broke. Then, under cover of a sandstorm, the Manchu cavalry rode around the flank and charged. Li's army broke and fled.

Li left Beijing a few days later, and Dorgon entered it on 5 June. The Qing declared that the right to rule had passed to them, and they conquered the south over the next decades. They ruled China until 1912.
